subject: octopus
pitch: A curious reef octopus in coral and rust tones, covered in little bumps and paler mottling. A soft, bulbous head, golden eyes with bar-shaped pupils and a slightly grumpy brow. Its eight arms curl out in every direction, each lined with rows of cream suckers, and one arm proudly holds up an old brass key it found on a shipwreck.
reasoning:
I'm planning the octopus rig without overengineering it: a bulbous mantle resting above the floor, arms splayed across the seabed with one raised to hold a key, and a skeleton rooted at a body joint with a head joint above and eight arm chains branching out.

Now I'm working out the geometry details -- curling arm paths tapering from thick bases to fine tips while keeping them above the floor, and a mantle swept along a chain that bulges outward then narrows toward the top, with eyes placed on the mantle's surface using angular positioning.

Writing mantle sweep code...

For texture, I'm planning a mottled coral-and-pale paint pattern with countershading, plus around 120 small scattered bumps in rust tones across the mantle, and roughly 192 sucker parts arranged in two rows per arm at specific angles so they stay visible rather than hidden against the floor.

Now I'm adding tiny sucker shapes using scaled-down cylinders in cream tones, building a wide flattened skirt where the arms meet the body, and setting up the loop to position each of the eight arms at evenly spaced angles around the body.

Tuning the arm path coordinates so the radius tapers smoothly toward the tip while keeping the y-height above the radius at every point, with odd arms curling upward slightly for variation.

I'm naming the arm joints with an indexed pattern like "arm01" through the chain length, and designating one front arm as a special tentacle that rises outward and upward with a curling tip, using distinct radius and height values at each control point along its path.

Now I'm working out how to place a brass key at the tip of that key-holding arm—building it from a ring bow, shaft, and bit sections, roughly 0.22 units long, oriented vertically and positioned so the arm's curling end wraps around the shaft near its midpoint.

Still working out coordinates...

Setting arm angles at 45° spacing with the key arm at index 0 (30°), I'm calculating lateral curl offsets and radial positions for each joint along the arms, then scaling down the max radius to keep the model from getting too wide for a stylized octopus.

For coloring, I'm layering a mottled coral-and-rust base paint with countershading toward a pale belly tone, then adding sparse pale spots on top for texture.

Now I'm placing suckers along the arm sweep, positioning them at angles for the visible sides of each arm and scaling their size based on the local arm radius at each point.

Now I'm scattering small rust bumps across the mantle and arm tops using filtered surface hits, then figuring out eye placement on the front-facing part of the mantle using azimuth and elevation offsets around a center point.

For the eyes themselves, I'm sticking golden spheres at those hit points, then adding a dark horizontal bar for pupils, positioning it just off the eye surface along the normal direction.

Working out the brow tilt...

I'll make the brow a flattened sphere scaled small in coral rust, positioned at the eye center offset along the hit normal and up vector. I'll skip the eyelid and socket ring for simplicity, and consider adding a small siphon cone at the body's front-bottom but may leave it out too.

Now I'm working out the mantle's geometry so the skirt bottom lands near y=0 and the sweep doesn't dip below ground—adjusting the starting y and radius of the mantle path and tweaking the radius keyframes so the tip rounds off properly near the top.

With the body height set around 0.58, I'm attaching the mantle chain and skirt to the body joint, then defining the arm chain's starting point inside the skirt radius. For the raised-arm pose, I'm computing key points along the arm's path using the angled offset vector, tracing from the shoulder up through intermediate radii toward a coiled approach near the target point K, where the final segment wraps around using sine/cosine offsets for the coil.

I'm working out the coil geometry by sampling angles from 180° through 90° at small vertical offsets from K, using Catmull-Rom interpolation across the points despite the sharp radius changes, and checking that the chain has enough joints per knot span to handle the tight coil curvature. I'm also tuning the radius taper along the arm—shrinking down near the tip and coil region—so the tube stays clear of the shaft's own radius, then deriving the tangent vector perpendicular to the offset direction to orient the coil properly.

Now I'm laying out the key's structure: a vertical shaft cylinder sized relative to K, a coil section above it, and a bow torus at the top rotated to face the viewer, plus small teeth boxes near the bottom offset outward to form the bit. I'm also planning to add a collar torus for decoration and apply a mottled brass-to-patina paint effect using a green mottle over the brass base color for aging detail.

Now I'm figuring out the positioning math—placing the key's top relative to K.y so it clears the mantle, and planning to anchor it to the last joint of the arm chain. I'm sketching a general arm-building function that takes joint points and radii, then setting up a loop to generate multiple curling tentacle-like arms with randomized curl directions and angles, reserving sucker details for the key-holding arm only.

Still writing arm geometry...

Now I'm adding a sucker placement function that samples points along the tentacle's surface at alternating angles and sticks cream-colored cylinder suckers scaled proportionally to the tentacle's local radius, working out the scale factor so each sucker's radius comes out to roughly 0.35 times the tentacle radius.

I'm swapping the cylinder for a torus shape instead, since a ring with a hollow center reads more visually as a sucker than a solid cylinder — rotating the torus geometry so it faces outward along the tentacle's normal rather than its default orientation, and sizing it so the outer radius lands around 0.34 times the local tentacle radius with a shallow embed depth.

For the mantle's bumpy texture I'm scattering small rust-colored sphere stick-ons across the surface, randomizing their scale a bit and flattening them against the body so they read as skin texture rather than protruding warts. I'm skipping the sand floor and siphon/funnel details as unnecessary, then moving on to building simple stick-based eyes with a warm yellow iris color and a dark pupil.

For the pupils, I'm positioning a thin dark box on each eye socket's surface using the hit point and normal, nudging it outward slightly so it sits flush against the curved eye sphere without sinking into it, then finalizing the color values and exporting the whole piece.
